WPT|/rc.tech.fld.title: Where the technology pays
WPT|/rc.tech.fld.sub: Fields in which the crystalline principle solves what a surface layer cannot — from the inside, on damp concrete, for good.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/0/1: From the inside, tested for drinking water (DVGW W 270 / W 347): no coating that could taint the water, 14 bar on the positive side, vapour permeable so the wall stays healthy. Filling after 3 days.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/1/1: The crystalline seal keeps the sludge in and the ground water out — after a water analysis of aggressive or soft water. Above the water line, where biogenic acid attacks the concrete, a resistant coating armours the concrete; the seal below stays.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/2/1: Against negative pressing water from the inside: no excavation, no disturbance of roads, gardens and neighbours. The wall keeps breathing, so plaster and room stay dry; moving cracks are injected first.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/3/1: Running leaks are stopped with {F20} in minutes, coves and cracks made good with {IM}, the pit sealed with {IC}: back in service quickly, walkable after about 5 hours, without pumps running for years.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/4/1: Against ground water from the accessible side; vapour permeable; abrasion, cleaning and surface wear do not remove the seal; no protection layer, no seams.
WPT|/rc.tech.fld/5/1: On the positive side: 14 bar, no membrane to protect from ice, debris and ultraviolet light; hairline cracks from temperature and shrinkage seal themselves for the life of the concrete.
WPT|/rc.lcc.label: Life-cycle cost
WPT|/rc.lcc.title: One application — or a renewal cycle
WPT|/rc.lcc.sub: Whole-life costing in the sense of ISO 15686-5: every cost that a waterproofing causes from its first application to the end of the planning horizon — application, protection layers, renewals with the access they need, upkeep. Set the model with your own rates: the defaults are relative planning values (installed cost of the crystalline system = 100 per m²), not quotations.
WPT|/rc.lcc.chart: Cumulative cost per m² over the planning horizon
WPT|/rc.lcc.verdict: Over {H} years the crystalline system costs {A} of the membrane and {B} of the resin coating (present value). Break-even against the membrane: {Y}.
WPT|/rc.lcc.why.title: Why the curves separate
WPT|/rc.lcc.why/0/1: The crystals are as durable as the concrete; there is no film to age, so nothing is re-applied. The upkeep is inspection.
WPT|/rc.lcc.why/1/1: From the inside there is no excavation, no road closure, no drainage to rebuild, no protection boards. Every renewal of an outside membrane pays that bill again.
WPT|/rc.lcc.why/2/1: Hairline cracks that would need a repair campaign on a film seal themselves: fewer interventions, no downtime of the tank or the pit.
WPT|/rc.lcc.why/3/1: Water kept out of the pores means chloride and carbon dioxide kept away from the reinforcement: the service life of the component itself is extended, which is the largest item of any life-cycle account.
WPT|/rc.lcc.note: Model, not a quotation. Nominal costs are summed as they fall due; present values discount every year’s cost at the rate set (ISO 15686-5). Downtime, risk of leaks and the extended service life of the structure are not priced in — they favour the crystalline system further. Replace the defaults by the rates of your project.

WPT|/wp.m3d.microNote: Micro scale: schematic close-up of a sectioned sample at the coating interface, not to scale. Each stage plays as a short animation.
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/ext: Micro scale shows the interface itself: the pores of the concrete, the matt damp surface, the first coat of {RB400} filling the pores, the second coat, and a crack opening under the coating that stays closed on top — the crack bridging of a flexible thick-layer coating.
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/inner: Micro scale shows the masonry skin with its salt-laden pores, the levelling, the rigid slurry {AQ1K} growing coat by coat, and water pressing from the rear that the slurry holds back (WTA 4-6, up to 0.75 bar).
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/negc: Micro scale shows the jetted concrete skin with its open pores, the pre-seal of {AQ1K} filling them, the two flexible coats of {RB400} over it, water pressing from the rear that the build-up holds back (WTA 4-6, up to 0.75 bar), and a fine crack of the concrete bridged by the flexible coating.
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/tank: Micro scale shows the smoothed concrete skin, the two coats of {RB400}, water standing on the coating, and a fine crack of the substrate bridged by the flexible coating.
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/balcony: Micro scale shows the primed screed, the joint sealing tape in its bed, the two coats of {AQ2K}, the tile adhesive and the tile — and a crack opening under the bonded waterproofing.
WPT|/wp.m3d.microSub/park: Micro scale shows the concrete skin with chloride-laden pores, the scratch coat of {OS} pressed into them, the two layers, and a moving crack bridged at −20 °C.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/ext/0/1: Sealing cove of {M30} (edge height 4–6 cm) on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K}; at the wall/slab transition the waterproofing is guided approx. 15 cm down onto the front face of the base slab; pipe penetrations with the sleeve bonded in {RB400} with the 4 mm notched trowel, fully overcoated.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/ext/1/1: {RB400} in a minimum of two application steps, free of pores, the second after approx. 3 hours: ≥ 2.0 mm dry film on concrete, ≥ 3.0 mm on masonry, ≥ 4.0 mm for pressing water W2.1-E.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/ext/2/1: Protection and drainage boards bonded with {RB400} and quartz sand 0.1–0.35 mm, buttering-floating. Rainproof after approx. 3 hours, 1 bar after approx. 16 hours, pressurised water after ≥ 1 day.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/inner/0/0: Salts and rising damp dealt with first
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/inner/0/1: Plaster off 80 cm beyond the damage, joints raked out 20 mm, levelled with {M30}; the retroactive horizontal barrier with {I380} or {AQF} stops the capillary transport.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/inner/1/0: The rigid slurry, coat by coat
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/inner/1/1: {AQ1K} brushed, trowelled or sprayed into the matt damp substrate, up to 1 mm per step, the second after approx. 6 hours; three steps for pressing water (up to 0.75 bar from the negative side).
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/inner/2/1: Keep damp ≥ 24 hours, no condensation, no direct heating; pressurised water after ≥ 7 days. The THERMOPAL restoration plaster stores salts and lets the wall breathe.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/negc/0/1: High-pressure water jetting lays the concrete bare; honeycombs broken out and filled with {M30}, the joint chased and filled, sealing cove; then {AQ1K} brushed in as pre-sealing — the rigid slurry keeps the moisture from the rear off the flexible coating.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/negc/1/1: The construction joint with {RB400} 15 cm on both sides to ≥ 4.0 mm dry film; then two coats over the face to ≥ 3.0 mm for water pressure, ≥ 2.0 mm for soil moisture (WTA 4-6); crack-bridging, radon-tight, watertight against negative pressing water to 0.75 bar.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/negc/2/1: Keep damp ≥ 3 days in dry rooms, ventilate deep pits, no condensation, no direct heating; 1 bar after approx. 16 hours, pressurised water after ≥ 1 day. Plaster, tiles or a coating may follow.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/tank/0/1: Jet-cleaned; voids re-profiled with {BIS540} on {HSF}, smoothed with {BIS16}; water-bearing cracks injected. The wall–floor junction with {RB400} and ASO-Dichtband-2000-S.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/tank/1/0: Two coats over walls and floor
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/tank/1/1: {RB400} by spray, brush or trowel, free of pores; ≥ 2.0 mm dry film for crack widths < 0.2 mm (W2-B), ≥ 4.0 mm for < 1.0 mm. {AQ2K} for chlorinated water, {AQ1K} for process and waste water.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/tank/2/1: Kept damp, condensation avoided with dryers; {RB400} withstands pressurised water after ≥ 1 day, the slurries after ≥ 7 days. Soft or aggressive water needs a water analysis (EN 1992-1-1).
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/balcony/0/1: ASO-Dichtband-2000 tapes, corners and sleeves bonded in {AQ2K} at the wall–floor joint, drains and intersections; movement joints with ASO-Dichtband-2000-S.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/balcony/1/1: {AQ2K} in two application steps of up to 1 mm, the second after approx. 3–6 hours; 3.5 kg/m² plus 25 % allowance (DIN 18531, DIN 18534). Crack bridging even at −5 °C.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/balcony/2/1: Tiles laid with a tile adhesive of the system list when the waterproofing has completely hardened; no point or linear loads on the coating itself.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/park/0/1: Concrete damaged by de-icing salt is milled off; the deck is blasted, matt damp; very absorbent substrates primed with {PRIM}.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/park/1/0: Scratch coat and first layer, wet in wet
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/park/1/1: {OS} pressed in as scratch coat and contact layer, the first layer immediately afterwards; up to 3 mm per step, approx. 1.8 kg/m² per mm.
WPT|/wp.m3d.co/park/2/1: Second layer after approx. 3 hours, approx. 5.5 kg/m² in total (OS 5b). Rainproof after 4 hours; chloride and CO₂ barrier, crack bridging class B2 at −20 °C.
WPT|/wp.lb/skirt: Coating turned 15 cm up the parapet
WPT|/wp.lb/drain: Drainage pipe in its gravel bed
WPT|/wp.lb/jetC: High-pressure water jetting, > 400 bar: paint and laitance off
WPT|/wp.lb/breakout: Chipping hammer: honeycomb broken out to sound concrete
WPT|/wp.lb/jointFill: Joint chased and filled with ASOCRET-M30
WPT|/wp.lb/preseal: Pre-sealed with AQUAFIN-1K against moisture from the rear
WPT|/wp.lb/bandC: Construction joint: AQUAFIN-RB400, 15 cm both sides, ≥ 4.0 mm
WPT|/wp.lb/chipT: Chipping hammer: old plaster taken off
WPT|/wp.lb/stripOff: Plaster removed ≥ 80 cm beyond the damage
WPT|/wp.lb/mill: Scarifier: salt-damaged skin milled off to the neutral zone
WPT|/wp.lb/blastH: Round the column, by hand: blast nozzle
WPT|/wp.lb/sleeve: Pipe sleeve bonded in RB400, no folds
WPT|/wp.lb/notch: RB400 with the 4 mm notched trowel
WPT|/wp.lb/dft: Dry film thickness to the class
WPT|/wp.lb/c2i: AQUAFIN-1K, second coat, after approx. 6 h
WPT|/wp.lb/c1t: RB400, first coat, walls and floor
WPT|/wp.lb/adhesive: Tile adhesive of the system list
WPT|/wp.lb/c1p: AQUAFIN-OS, first layer, wet in wet
